Section A's stated constraint (the guard sees only reviewer + current_state and must load nothing) is checked against the real function at cli/review.py:186 and holds — it takes `cs` and reads only `current_state`, and all 8 call sites run it before governance/packets are loaded, so a static (reviewer, state) -> command mapping is the only design that respects it. Section C's separation is the load-bearing architectural call and it is correct: derive_independence counts review_budget_exceeded for ANY reviewer (engineering/attestation.py:359-365) while the classification block above it is code-review-scoped by design 4.1, so attaching the count to _independence_line would render a plan-review hold as a code-review claim. Putting it on its own per-slug line in the same human-path region as the existing _independence_line and `gate bypass:` loops (cli/attest.py:222-234) matches the ownership already there. Failure paths unchanged: every addition is disclosure-only and cannot flip attest verify's pass/fail.

str.isprintable() is the right predicate rather than a hand-rolled control-character set: ASCII space is printable in Python so multi-word ids keep working, while newline, C0/C1, U+2028 and zero-width characters all fail — exactly the class that corrupts a prompt line, a JSON enum and a digest simultaneously (the three consumers named in review_checklist.py:35-37). Rejecting at resolve_checklist sits beside the two existing loud guards (non-string list, empty list) rather than introducing a silently-tolerant escaping path, and resolve_checklist has exactly one caller (core/review_bundle.py:145), so raising has no blast radius into read paths. Section D's frozenset-vs-list hazard is real (_model_qualifiers returns frozenset at cli/review.py:1402, compared with `<=` at line 1447) and the chosen row discriminates: subset gives True (no contradiction) while list comparison of ["[beta]"] <= ["[1m]", "[beta]"] gives False (contradiction), so the row fails if the container type changes. I re-derived the issue's own proposed row and confirmed the plan's claim that it passes under both semantics.
